newsitem.title: GERMANY: Strong British currency deters German cocoa buyers.
newsitem.headline: Strong British currency deters German cocoa buyers.

text.p: Cocoa buying from Germany's chocolate industry remains hampered by the strong pound although the latest slide in futures should be tempting, traders said on Wednesday.
"The industry is producing at high levels and would like to take cover but it is under extreme profit pressure and raw materials buyers are extremely cautious," one said.
"Possible gains from lower futures are offset by the high sterling level and that paralyses the market."
Demand for cocoa butter was also patchy.
Traders said high manufacturing activity was partly a result of an early Easter holiday this year, a consumption peak which will fall into the first quarter.
Cocoa grindings should be strong in the first three months but the industry was not very optimistic for the rest of the year as export chances to eastern Europe also looked uncertain.
Traders said strong cocoa arrivals at origin belied recent deficit forecasts for 1996/97 -- one from the ICCO at 225,000 tonnes and another from trader Man at 170,000-230,000.
"These figures won't make any difference unless the tightness can actually be felt, and that's not at all the case," another trader said.
"Sellers are coming in all the time -- even Ghana has dropped its usual premium over futures."
Feb/March cif Ivorian bean sellers were slightly lower than last week at 2.29-2.31 marks per kg (2.33), but consumers' buying ideas were at 2.20-2.22.
The first quarter cocoa butter ratio was unchanged at 2.66 and implied mark prices liquid ex-works were 6.26 marks (6.30).
Sterling was at 2.6757 marks at the Frankfurt Exchange Fixing at midday.
